sentences: Revolving credit utilization is the most important driver of predicted default, accounting for about 27% of the model's importance, and predicted risk rises steadily as utilization goes up.
The number of past delinquencies is the second most important driver, and risk rises as delinquencies accumulate.
The two drivers interact strongly: the effect of utilization is much larger for applicants with two past delinquencies than for those with none, so the two together matter more than either alone.
Income has a moderate effect, with higher income associated with lower predicted risk.
Length of credit history has a moderate effect, with longer histories associated with lower predicted risk, though this effect is weaker for applicants with many recent inquiries.
The debt-to-income ratio has a weak effect, with higher ratios associated with somewhat higher risk.
The data do not settle whether feature_a, feature_b and age have any consistent direction of effect, and each of them has a negligible share of importance.
Recent credit inquiries have a weak effect, with three or more inquiries adding a small amount to predicted risk.
